claim: CodeVetter can retain a closed, bounded inventory of framework-emitted Next request phases and can reject those phases as the bottleneck when they do not cross deterministic absolute and parent-share thresholds.

implementation_evidence.capture_surface: NEXT_OTEL_PERFORMANCE_PREFIX-backed performance measures in an owned config-disabled Next runtime
discarded_values: route or application values from the measure

proofs: Only allowlisted framework phase names under the fixed owned prefix are retained.
Static requests, unrelated requests, out-of-request measures, private detail, and unknown names are excluded.
Phase order, bounds, interval-union overlap, and incomplete-inventory refusal are deterministic.
A material phase can produce a source-null, edit-ineligible hypothesis without changing child accounting.

flow.name: home renders
flow.failure_boundary: The existing exact assertion did not pass before the bounded timeout; runtime evidence remains diagnostic only.

diagnosis.result: All retained phases were below both the 5 ms absolute and 20% request-share thresholds, so CodeVetter rejected this framework-phase family as the observed bottleneck.

limitations: The closed phase inventory is not a complete Next request critical path; unexposed framework work remains possible.
Phase intervals are not added to or subtracted from supported child-operation accounting.
The real product run used a local config-disabled Next development runtime and does not establish production performance.
The existing exact Playwright assertion did not pass within the bounded timeout, so this capture authorizes no optimization or source edit.
The sampled Playwright-plus-Next process tree peak is diagnostic-run overhead, not application steady-state memory.
